neighbours.label: the word right after a relational determiner (the other / the same / much / next) that picks out something relative to a reference
fire: The bakery on the other side of the square sells better bread.
Sales were up four percent compared with the same month a year ago.
The second exam was much harder than the first one we took.
We swam across the lake and rested on the other shore for an hour.
Rents in the city rose at the same rate as wages last decade.
The new bridge is much longer than the old wooden one it replaced.
She kept one glove and lost the other half of the pair on the bus.
The film's sequel did much better at the box office than expected.
quiet: The bakery on the corner of the square sells better bread.
Sales were up four percent compared with a year ago.
The second exam was harder, as the first one had warned us.
We swam across the lake and rested on the shore for an hour.
Rents in the city rose quickly while wages stalled last decade.
The new bridge is long and painted a bright shade of red.
She kept one glove and lost her scarf on the bus.
The film's sequel did well at the box office, as expected.

predictions: 5/8 fire; the same sentences without the relational word stay quieter
notes: Probe: 'the other part of the trail' 0.825, 'much more complicated' 0.495, 'the same quarter' 0.380, 'the next day' 0.233; removing the relational word: 0.121, 0.079, 0.091. 'looked the other way' only 0.094, so not every 'other' fires. Card density 0.47%.
